jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE As an EM for Semgrep's supply chain team, you’ll lead a team building customer-facing tools to help developers secure their software from vulnerabilities introduced by dependencies. Other supply chain management tools exist, but they produce far too much noise to be useful or efficient. Security teams may review thousands of vulnerabilities, informing developers that hundreds of their dependencies have introduced critical vulnerabilities and need updating, when in reality they are not even using those dependencies in a vulnerable way. Perhaps you’ve even felt this pain yourself! Our goal is to cut through the noise: to make it easy to find and remediate the 20% of vulnerabilities that are actually reachable given the way our customers’ use their dependencies. We work to make supply chain security as simple and intuitive for our users as possible so developers can focus on their own mission. Semgrep's detection teams own best-in-class SAST, secrets, SCA, and malware engines; Guardian owns the integration, orchestration, and distribution that turn them into a single, low-latency risk verdict an agent or developer can act on in the moment. That one change is why Automation Engineering is becoming the operating model for enterprise services, and why service teams stop being a bottleneck and start being an advantage. As an Automation Engineer, you build Serval's agents directly into the customer's instance, and the tickets stop arriving: onboarding, access requests, approvals, the long tail that clogs a service desk. You'll push Serval past its current limits into new use cases, dogfood unreleased features, bring field ideas back to our product team, and act as a practitioner evangelist for both Serval and Automation Engineering. This is a title we are coining. Nobody has ten years of it yet, so what you build becomes the standard for everyone after you. jobs.title: Hardware Diagnostics Engineer - Infrastructure
jobs.description_text: About the Role We are looking for a Hardware Diagnostics Engineer to run burn-in, triage what fails, work servers out-of-band, and own RMAs end to end. If you like hardware that misbehaves in ways that take real work to explain, this is a good seat. Before any GPU server carries a customer workload, it has to prove it works — under load, at temperature, for hours. When it doesn't, somebody has to figure out why, get replacement hardware in, and send the failed part back to the vendor. What You’ll Do - Run server and GPU burn-in and stress testing, interpret the results, and decide whether hardware is production-ready - Triage failures across GPUs, memory, drives, NICs, PSUs, and cabling: reproduce the failure, isolate the faulty component, and document what proved it - Work servers out-of-band through IPMI and Redfish for power control, boot configuration, BIOS settings, and sensor and event log collection - Apply firmware updates across the fleet following the team's qualified baselines and rollout process - Drive RMAs with vendors from ticket through replacement, installation, and return of the failed part - Keep asset, serial, and replacement history accurate in NetBox so we know what's actually in every rack - Track failure patterns across the fleet and raise them when the same part or firmware version keeps turning up - Improve the runbooks you work from, and script the steps you find yourself repeating - Partner with datacenter operations on hands-on work during turn-up

While we can’t reveal too much just yet, our team is tackling cutting-edge engineering challenges to bring revolutionary products to life. About the Role We're looking for an upstart University Recruitment Ambassador Intern who brings a strong blend of customer service and operations skills to help us build a world class data collection program. You will find candidates who match our study requirements and build a pipeline to our data collection studies. You'll also serve as a friendly point of contact for participants as they move through the process, fostering a community of folks interested in advancing new techology. If you enjoy talking to people and have a passion for technology this role is for you! jobs.title: Software Engineer, Real-Time Generalist
jobs.description_text: The Opportunity Most full stack roles ask you to move pixels around a dashboard. This one asks you to help architect the system that controls the largest drone swarm on the planet. You’ll join the team building Legion, Swarm Aero’s Command & Control platform. Legion enables a single operator to plan, direct, and execute missions across a networked swarm of heterogeneous aircraft in real time, over intermittent communications, and at a scale nobody else in the industry is attempting. This is not a role maintaining a finished product or adding features around the edges. You’ll help define the architecture, establish core technical patterns, and build entirely new capabilities for a problem space with little prior art. The work spans real-time distributed systems, dense telemetry visualization, collaborative mission planning, and operator interfaces where clarity and reliability directly affect mission outcomes. You’ll have meaningful influence over what we build, how we build it, and how the platform evolves as the team and system scale. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Help architect and build the full stack of a Command & Control system directing large swarms of heterogeneous aircraft - Design the foundational systems, technical patterns, and interfaces that will shape Legion as it scales - Build collaborative, real-time infrastructure that allows operators to control large numbers of aircraft simultaneously, including through degraded or intermittent communications - Create new ways to repr

jobs.description_text: About the Role Our avionics system is built and running on aircraft hardware. We're looking for an experienced Embedded Software Engineer to join our avionics team and own that work. You'll write real-time embedded software that directly controls aircraft systems, from flight control and sensor integration to communication protocols. This is safety-critical software on hardware that flies, and the surface keeps growing. jobs.title: Structures Design Engineer, Airframe
jobs.description_text: About this Role We are building a Group 5 autonomous aircraft and driving it to first flight. We are in detailed design with tooling in work, and we are looking for a structures design engineer to own parts on that aircraft from concept through first article. You will design and size real hardware: control surfaces, ribs and spars, frames, doors and access panels, fittings and joints. You will take your parts all the way out, through analysis, drawings, vendor coordination, first article, and the fixes that come after. Our structures lead sets the architecture and the design approach. Inside that, your parts are yours. This is a role for someone who wants to design more and coordinate less. You will be in CAD and in FEA most days, and in the shop the rest of them. The aircraft is small enough as an organization that the person who draws a part is the person who sees it come off the tool, and finds out the same week whether the call they made was right. The right person needs to be comfortable moving between implementation and documentation. This is not just a paperwork role. They need to understand how AWS is architected, how controls are actually implemented, how to produce evidence, how to drive remediation, and how to keep the broader security program aligned as Legion moves into IL5/IL6 environments. You’ll own the development of hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) test systems and functional testers for our autonomous aircraft’s avionics. That means designing test architectures, building fixtures and interfaces, writing automation, and putting real hardware through realistic operating conditions. Your work will help engineers find problems earlier and give manufacturing repeatable ways to verify every unit we build. This is a hands-on engineering role with scope from the first bench setup through aircraft integration and production. jobs.description_text: The Role Accounting at a company like ours is not a steady-state job. We buy parts, build aircraft, and sign contracts with the government, often all in the same month. Every one of those activities has to be recorded correctly, supportable under audit, and structured so it still holds up when we're ten times bigger. We're looking for an accountant who wants to own that. You'll run the close, keep the ledger clean, and be the person who figures out the right treatment when something new shows up, which will happen often. You'll help set up the cost structures, controls, and processes the company will run on for years. This is a senior role, and we care more about how you think than how long you've been doing it. If you've built real depth early and you're ready for more ownership than your current seat allows, we want to hear from you. You'll work closely with finance leadership and partner with operations, supply chain, and our program teams. What You'll Do - Own the month-end close: journal entries, accruals, reconciliations, and the schedules that support them - Keep the general ledger accurate, timely, and something an auditor could walk through without surprises - Account for inventory as we move from prototypes to production: raw materials, WIP, finished goods, capitalization, and cost of goods sold - Help build and maintain our cost structure for government contracts, including indirect cost pools, allocation bases, rate tracking, and segregation of unallowable costs -

jobs.title: Senior/Staff System Research Engineer – LLM Inference Optimization
jobs.description_text: We are looking for talented systems developers and researchers to join the Snowflake AI Research team and advance the state of the art in LLM inference systems and optimization. Our mission is to build the next generation of high-performance and intelligent inference systems. We optimize not only how fast and efficiently models run, but also how quickly inference systems can adapt to new models, architectures, hardware, and workloads. Our work spans the full inference stack—from distributed serving and runtime systems to GPU kernels and model-system co-design. We explore techniques such as adaptive parallelism, speculative and parallel decoding, disaggregated inference, scheduling and batching, KV-cache optimization, model swapping, quantization, and GPU kernel optimization to push the frontier of latency, throughput, scalability, and cost. Beyond optimizing individual models, we are building intelligent and adaptive inference systems that can automate performance optimization—rapidly profiling new models and workloads, identifying bottlenecks, selecting effective execution strategies, and adapting system configurations with minimal manual tuning. We embrace AI-native engineering, using AI not only as the workload we optimize, but also as a tool to accelerate system development, experimentation, debugging, optimization, and adaptation to new models. Our goal is to accelerate both the speed of inference and the agility of inference development. This is an exciting opportunity

jobs.title: Sales Compensation Manager (12-Month Fixed-Term Contract)
jobs.description_text: YOUR MISSION As a Sales Compensation Program Manager, you will own the end-to-end design, delivery, and governance of UiPath's sales incentive programs. You will lead annual plan design and rollout, oversee monthly commission processing and payout accuracy, manage Xactly system administration and configuration roadmaps, and partner with Sales, Finance, HR, and Operations leadership to ensure compensation plans drive the right selling behaviors. Deep, hands-on experience with Xactly Incent is required. The ideal candidate is a strategic, data-driven leader with strong execution skills who can translate business objectives into clear, motivating, and cost-effective incentive plans. You will be accountable for on-time and accurate payouts, sound plan governance and controls, and clear communication of plan mechanics to the field. Reporting to the Head of Global Sales Compensation, you will guide and mentor Sales Compensation Analysts and serve as a trusted advisor to sales leaders. Additionally, you will partner closely with Sales Operations, Finance, and the Sales Business Intelligence & Reporting team on quota setting, territory and portfolio management, and commission expense forecasting. Please note: 1. This is a 12-month fixed-term contract, with the possibility of extension depending on performance and business needs. 2. jobs.title: Senior Sales Compensation Analyst (12-Month Fixed-Term Contract)
jobs.description_text: Your mission As a Sales Compensation Program Analyst, you will be primarily focused on the delivery and successful execution of sales incentive plans. You will be responsible for supporting the design, system configuration, running monthly reports on sales performance actuals, preparing compensation payout analysis, maintaining compensation documents, providing new hire support, and partnering with internal team members to review requirements, design solutions, configure and test system deliverables. Hands-on configuration experience and knowledge of Xactly or similar Sales Performance Management tool is required. You will highlight risks and opportunities within the compensation team, working closely with the Head of Global Sales Compensation and Program Managers to provide overall business support to the business’ sales & operations teams. Additionally, you will contribute in supporting portfolio and territory management, quota design, and partnering with the Sales Business Intelligence & Reporting team to provide Sales reporting. Please note: This is a 12-month fixed-term contract, with the possibility of extension depending on performance and business needs. The ideal candidate is a data-driven problem solver with top-notch execution skills who will work cross-functionally with the Sales, Finance, HR and Operations teams. jobs.description_text: WHAT YOU WILL DO AT UIPATH - Work in a central team with other engineers and product managers, to envision and deliver organization wide engineering services - Create Kubernetes infrastructure, design and built continuously reconciled systems, contribute both imperative and declarative code - Bring the best that the community has to offer on agile software development and continuous deployment - Enhance observance and propose enforcement mechanisms of best practices across the engineering organizations - Collaborate with internal teams to identify business goals, technical requirements, and implement solutions to maximize automation and efficiency - Improve CI/CD processes, bring about innovation - What you will bring to UiPath - A strong fundamental understanding of Computer Science through pursuit of a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD degree in Computer Science, math, or a related discipline - An inclination towards best practices, following community trends while adhering to their theoretical underpinnings - Programming knowledge in one or more object-oriented languages (such as C#/C++/Java). Experience in Golang is a bonus - Experience from previous internships or other multi-person projects, including open-source contributions.
